limitations_and_boundaries: The study uses organotypic culture models and may not fully recapitulate in vivo tumor microenvironment complexity.
Clinical sample analysis is limited to head and neck SCCs; generalizability to other cancer types is not established.
The study does not address the role of immune cells or other stromal components in collective invasion.
Rescue experiments (e.g., restoring track formation after inhibition) were not performed to confirm sufficiency of identified pathways.

research_questions.statement: How do stromal fibroblasts and carcinoma cells cooperate during collective invasion, and what are the molecular requirements in leading versus following cells?

additional_provenance.text_excerpt: Fibroblast-led collective invasion of carcinoma cells with differing roles for RhoGTPases in leading and following cells

provenance.text_excerpt: the physical generation of tracks through the combined action of force- and protease-mediated matrix remodelling is crucial

claims.statement: Stromal fibroblasts lead collective invasion of carcinoma cells by generating physical tracks in the ECM through force-mediated and protease-mediated matrix remodeling.

additional_provenance.text_excerpt: the requirement for integrins α3 or α5 is confined to the leading fibroblast in collectively invading cocultures

provenance.text_excerpt: Rho–ROCK function is required in leading fibroblasts but not following cancer cells

claims.statement: Rho-ROCK signaling and integrins α3/α5 are required in leading fibroblasts for force-mediated matrix remodeling and track formation, but not in following carcinoma cells.

additional_provenance.text_excerpt: neither protease nor Rho function is required in the carcinoma cells. Instead, they use the related small G-protein Cdc42 to regulate actomyosin organization and generate the force needed to follow the tracks generated by stromal fibroblasts

provenance.text_excerpt: Cdc42 and MRCK function in cancer cells is required to follow fibroblasts

claims.statement: Carcinoma cells use Cdc42 and MRCK to regulate actomyosin organization and follow tracks generated by fibroblasts, without requiring Rho, MMP, or integrin α3/α5 function.

datasets.description: SCC12 or A431 cells cultured on collagen I/Matrigel matrix with or without HN-CAFs or V-CAFs; invasion quantified after 7 days.
datasets.name: Organotypic invasion assays

datasets.description: Frozen sections from head and neck SCCs analyzed for collagen, fibronectin, and active Rho.
datasets.name: Clinical head and neck SCC samples

evidence_spans.content: Cancer cells with mesenchymal characteristics (HT1080) invaded equally well in the absence or presence of fibroblasts.

provenance.text_excerpt: Cancer cells with mesenchymal characteristics (HT1080 fibrosarcoma cells) invaded equally well in the absence or presence of fibroblasts

evidence_spans.content: Integrin α5 was frequently upregulated in stromal fibroblasts in clinical SCC samples.

provenance.text_excerpt: integrin α5 was frequently upregulated in stromal fibroblasts in clinical SCC samples

evidence_spans.content: RhoA, but not RhoB, is required for fibroblasts to promote SCC invasion.

provenance.text_excerpt: RhoA, but not RhoB, is required for fibroblasts to promote SCC invasion

evidence_spans.content: SCC cells always invaded as collective chains and retained expression of epithelial markers, such as E-cadherin and p120 catenin.

provenance.text_excerpt: SCC cells always invaded as collective chains and retained expression of epithelial markers, such as E-cadherin and p120 catenin

evidence_spans.content: Soluble factors are not responsible for fibroblast-stimulated invasion; physical conditioning of the ECM promotes SCC invasion.

provenance.text_excerpt: soluble factors are not responsible for fibroblast-stimulated invasion of SCC cells and suggest that physical conditioning of the ECM can promote the invasion of SCCs

experiments_or_tasks: Collagen contraction assay to quantify force-mediated matrix remodeling.
Histochemical analysis of clinical head and neck SCC samples for collagen bundling, fibronectin deposition, and active Rho (RBD probe).
Multi-photon confocal time-lapse imaging to track cell motility and invasion.
Organotypic culture of SCC cells with or without carcinoma-associated fibroblasts (CAFs) to assess invasion.
Pharmacological inhibition of Rho (Tat C3), ROCK (Y27632), non-muscle myosin (blebbistatin), and MMPs (GM6001) to assess track formation and invasion.
Removal of fibroblasts after matrix remodeling to test if physical tracks are sufficient for SCC invasion.
siRNA knockdown of Rho, ROCK1/2, integrin α3, integrin α5, Cdc42, and MRCKα/β in specific cell types.

methods.name: Organotypic culture
methods.protocol_description: 5×10^5 HN-CAFs embedded in collagen I (4.6 mg/ml) and Matrigel (2.2 mg/ml); 5×10^5 SCC12 cells plated on top; cultures fed from below with complete media changed daily; fixed after 7 days for H&E staining.

methods.name: Time-lapse imaging
methods.protocol_description: Multi-photon confocal microscopy of organotypic cultures; GFP and mRFP excited at 488 nm or 870 nm; collagen imaged by reflectance or second harmonic generation.

methods.name: Fibroblast removal assay
methods.protocol_description: After 5 days, fibroblasts killed with puromycin (5 µg/ml for 48 h) or extraction buffer (0.5% Triton-X100, 20 mM NH4OH in PBS); then SCC12 cells plated on top.

methods.name: Collagen contraction assay
methods.protocol_description: 5×10^5 HN-CAFs embedded in matrix; after 4 days, gel diameter measured; contraction percentage = 100×(well diameter - gel diameter)/well diameter.

methods.name: siRNA transfection
methods.protocol_description: Cells plated at 60% confluence; transfected with 100 nM siRNA using DharmaFECT 2 (SCC cells) or DharmaFECT 1 (fibroblasts).

methods.name: Histochemical analysis
methods.protocol_description: Frozen sections fixed in 4% PFA, permeabilized with 0.2% Triton X-100, blocked with 5% FBS; incubated with GFP-RBD probe (0.05 µg/ml) or antibodies; collagen visualized by second harmonic generation.

study_units.name: Fibroblast-led collective invasion and matrix remodeling

provenance.text_excerpt: The extent of invasion was dependent on the number of fibroblasts introduced into the matrix

results.value_raw_text: The extent of invasion was dependent on the number of fibroblasts introduced into the matrix.

provenance.text_excerpt: blockade of Rho or ROCK1 and ROCK2 function only in fibroblasts prevented the invasion of SCC12 cells. Interestingly, inhibition of Rho or ROCK1 and ROCK2 in SCC12 cells did not affect the ability of SCC12 cells to invade in the presence of fibroblasts

results.value_raw_text: Blockade of Rho or ROCK1/2 only in fibroblasts prevented SCC12 invasion; inhibition in SCC12 cells did not affect invasion.

provenance.text_excerpt: To evaluate the activity of Rho proteins in the clinical samples, we used an affinity probe, based on the Rho-binding domain (RBD) of rhotekin, which only binds to Rho in its active conformation

results.value_raw_text: Active Rho was detected in stromal fibroblasts in clinical SCC samples using RBD probe; control probe showed poor binding.

provenance.text_excerpt: in collectively invading chains of SCC cells, MLC was clearly localized to regions of the cell cortex in contact with the ECM

results.value_raw_text: In collectively invading chains of SCC cells, MLC was localized to regions of the cell cortex in contact with the ECM.

provenance.text_excerpt: SCC cells were motile, even in the absence of fibroblasts, and their motility was not significantly changed in the presence of fibroblasts

results.value_raw_text: SCC cells were motile even in the absence of fibroblasts, and motility was not significantly changed in the presence of fibroblasts.

provenance.text_excerpt: Control fibroblasts were shown to contract the matrix over a number of days, typically by 16%, whereas Rho or ROCK inhibition reduced this to <5%

results.value_raw_text: Control fibroblasts contracted the matrix by 16%; Rho or ROCK inhibition reduced contraction to <5%.

provenance.text_excerpt: Introduction of fibroblasts isolated from either oral or vulval squamous cell carcinomas (HN-CAF or V-CAF, respectively) into the matrix caused two different SCC cell lines (SCC12 and A431), but not untransformed keratinocytes (HaCAT), to invade

results.value_raw_text: SCC12 and A431 cells invade into matrix only when fibroblasts are present; untransformed HaCAT do not invade.

provenance.text_excerpt: blockade of Rho (Tat C3), ROCK (Y27632) or non-muscle myosin (blebbistatin) function prevented the formation of holes in the ECM and concentration of matrix around the cells

results.value_raw_text: Blockade of Rho (Tat C3), ROCK (Y27632), non-muscle myosin (blebbistatin), or MMP (GM6001) prevented formation of holes in the ECM and concentration of matrix around cells.

provenance.text_excerpt: siRNA-mediated knockdown of either Cdc42 or both MRCK isoforms clearly disrupted the localization and phosphorylation of MLC at the cortex of SCC cells

results.value_raw_text: siRNA-mediated knockdown of Cdc42 or both MRCK isoforms disrupted localization and phosphorylation of MLC at the cortex of SCC cells.

provenance.text_excerpt: interference with either Cdc42 or MRCK in the SCC cells blocked their ability to invade in response to stromal fibroblasts

results.value_raw_text: Interference with either Cdc42 or MRCK in SCC cells blocked their ability to invade in response to stromal fibroblasts.

results.metric_name: Invasion after fibroblast removal and prior inhibition

provenance.text_excerpt: blockade of either Rho or ROCK function in the fibroblasts was sufficient to prevent the invasion of untreated SCC cells. In addition, inhibition of MMP function in the fibroblasts before the addition of SCC cells also prevented the invasion of SCC cells... When fibroblasts had been allowed to remodel the matrix before being removed, then the invasion of SCC cells was no longer blocked by inhibition of MMP or Rho function

results.value_raw_text: When fibroblasts were removed after matrix remodeling, SCC invasion was blocked if Rho, ROCK, or MMP were inhibited in fibroblasts before removal; but after remodeling, SCC invasion was no longer blocked by MMP or Rho inhibition.

provenance.text_excerpt: siRNA-mediated depletion of either integrin α3 or integrin α5 in stromal fibroblasts, but not in SCC cells, reduced the collective invasion of SCC cells

results.value_raw_text: siRNA-mediated depletion of integrin α3 or integrin α5 in stromal fibroblasts, but not in SCC cells, reduced collective invasion of SCC cells.

provenance.text_excerpt: Invading fibroblasts generate tracks in the matrix that are characterized by thick collagen bundles around their sides and an absence of matrix in their centre

results.value_raw_text: Fibroblasts generate tracks in the matrix characterized by thick collagen bundles around their sides and an absence of matrix in their centre.
